objective: Bind long-running delegated-task status transitions, progress, cancellation, checkpoint lineage, trace position, terminal results, replay protection, and explicit non-authority semantics to an admitted cross-agent handoff without executing remote work.

research_inputs.finding: A2A provides provider-neutral communication for opaque agents, Agent Cards, synchronous and streaming interactions, asynchronous notifications, rich artifacts, and long-running collaboration without exposing internal memory or tools.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds lifecycle receipts around admitted handoffs while preserving opacity and preventing Agent Card or remote-result metadata from becoming authority.

research_inputs.finding: MCP defines stateless requests, capability negotiation, progress, cancellation, and opt-in asynchronous Tasks with durable handles; tool descriptions and annotations require explicit trust controls.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The lifecycle state machine models bounded progress, cancellation, durable receipt state, and explicit non-authority flags without importing MCP as a privileged dependency.

research_inputs.finding: The Agents SDK guidance separates orchestration, handoffs, guardrails, resumable approval flows, tracing, sessions, sandbox workspaces, and evaluation.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL binds lifecycle transitions to existing handoff, checkpoint, and trace boundaries while keeping execution and approval outside this receipt module.

research_inputs.finding: The SDK exposes resumable run state, tracing, handoffs, MCP integration, sessions, sandbox agents, and human-in-the-loop controls as runtime features.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The contract provides provider-neutral evidence for resumable delegated task state and terminal result linkage without depending on a provider SDK.

features: bounded task expiry and generation fencing
admitted, running, paused, cancel-requested, cancelled, completed, and failed states
monotonic trace positions and non-regressing progress
checkpoint digest required for pause and advancing checkpoint lineage
terminal result digest required for completion
replay protection and task-record body tamper detection

measured_validation.comparison_interpretation: The lifecycle admission path is slower than the prior handoff-only receipt because it adds task record integrity, lifecycle state, and event-lineage fields. This is a control-plane overhead measurement, not an end-to-end agent performance claim.

limitations: The module is a bounded userspace/control-plane receipt contract; it does not execute tasks, contact remote agents, transport A2A or MCP messages, invoke models, or mint credentials.
Identity, handoff digest, checkpoint digest, result digest, and timestamps are caller-supplied evidence and are not independently hardware-attested or externally signed by this local implementation.
The benchmark measures local Python receipt overhead and excludes network, storage, model, accelerator, and kernel latency.

The snapshot-index adjacent regression was not claimed as passed because its long fixture exceeded the bounded execution window after emitting earlier successful markers; the other ten adjacent suites passed.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, production KMS, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, superiority to Linux, or resolution of existing external release blockers.
